title: dirt
meta_description: Dirt is the first marketable juke32 mp3 player, featuring a simple control disc, USB-C, 3.5mm output, and a micro SD card slot.

sections.heading: dirt : a juke32 mp3 player
sections.content: The first model given a name for being marketable.

sections.heading: features
items: Simple control disc for power, volume, and track selection

sections.heading: why not dirt?
items: SD cards are too expensive to buy in bulk (do not buy cheap micro sd cards, they die very quickly)
Too many wires to strip and solder
No mechanical design could reliably control power, volume, and track selection
No indicator to differentiate between the box being off vs. idle
Uses too much power on idle
No room for battery / unsafe where I could put it (unless I change dimensions)
Natural differences in wood and switch thickness

sections.heading: notes
sections.content: The control disc was a great concept but proved difficult to implement due to not finding low-travel small latching switches. The varying dimensions of stuff I did buy also made designing challenging.

The project devolved into rapid iteration (guessing and checking). Having to engrave/cut 3 different thicknesses of wood just to make my design work. (no 3d printer to make this easier) The process was tedious and there were too many unknowns to account for.
Why couldn't I just buy some board that already has a switch and battery management circuit? I did just that with Lapis
